A professional 3x3 grid location reference sheet for film production, showing 9 distinct views of the same location in consistent visual style.

[LOCATION]:
INT. WALK-UP APARTMENT, KITCHEN COUNTER — LATE AFTERNOON - LATE AFTERNOON
Type: Interior

[VISUAL DESCRIPTION]:
A cramped New York walk-up kitchen reduced, in frame, to a stretch of bone-white laminate counter. Hard afternoon window light rakes across the surface, throwing clean hard-edged shadows from a cracked flip phone, a folded napkin set list, two subway tokens, half a bagel and a squat coral lipstick tube. Beyond the counter, out of focus, sit an old enamel sink, a kettle and a chipped tile backsplash. Also seen as a hero-product frame lit by direct on-camera flash.

[ARCHITECTURAL STYLE]:
Pre-war New York tenement walk-up; utilitarian small-space kitchen with old fixtures and painted-over trim

[KEY FEATURES]:
Bone-white laminate counter, hard window light shadows, chipped subway-tile backsplash, cracked flip phone, napkin set list, subway tokens, half bagel

[COLOR PALETTE]:
Bone white, oat beige, warm cream with a single saturated coral accent

[LIGHTING]:
Hard directional window daylight from camera left creating crisp shadows; alternate direct on-camera flash for hero frames

[ATMOSPHERE]:
Quiet, clean, pre-departure stillness with a graphic editorial precision

[STYLE DIRECTION]:
Render this location in the following visual style:
Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
Lighting direction: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
Camera approach: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
Reference look: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content.
All 9 panels must consistently reflect this style direction.
[GRID LAYOUT - 3 rows × 3 columns, each panel 16:9 aspect ratio]:

Row 1 - ESTABLISHING SHOTS:
- Panel 1 (Top-Left): Wide exterior/approach view showing the location in context
- Panel 2 (Top-Center): Main establishing shot - the primary view of the location
- Panel 3 (Top-Right): Alternate angle establishing shot

Row 2 - MEDIUM SHOTS:
- Panel 4 (Middle-Left): Key interior/exterior area view
- Panel 5 (Middle-Center): Central focal point of the location
- Panel 6 (Middle-Right): Secondary important area

Row 3 - DETAIL & ATMOSPHERE:
- Panel 7 (Bottom-Left): Architectural or design details close-up
- Panel 8 (Bottom-Center): Texture and material details
